- When sentiment is consistently low or neutral (≤0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 2-period moving average.
- If sentiment rises steadily (≥0.4 over 3+ days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecasted values.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is weak but recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves); adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is rising but price is flat or falling, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” traps.
- When sentiment is high but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize reversal; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to prevent “sentiment lag” bias.
